metadata.title: AI, Agentic Commerce and the New Rules of Chargeback Management

content.text:
With first-party fraud and friendly disputes eroding already thin retail margins, managing chargebacks requires far more than basic operational recovery. Here, Tim Tynan, CEO of Chargeback Gurus, discusses how local AI streamlines dispute documentation, why fighting invalid chargebacks won't destroy legitimate customer relationships and how retailers must adapt their risk protocols for new protocols like Visa's Trusted Agent and Google's AP2.
Sourcing Journal: First-party fraud and chargebacks continue to erode thin merchant margins. What major forces—from evolving consumer behavior to shifting card network rules—are making chargeback management uniquely complex for merchants right now?
Tim Tynan: There are a few different things making chargeback management more complicated. Shopping is happening across more channels and payment methods, including emerging developments such as agentic payments. Consumers can dispute purchases more easily, and the overall volume of disputes is growing. Mastercard sponsored some research by Datos Insights that projects global chargeback volume will grow 24 percent by 2028. That puts additional pressure on merchants to find ways to manage chargebacks more efficiently.
SJ: Merchants often struggle to balance fraud mitigation with maintaining a seamless customer experience. How do unresolved chargebacks and aggressive dispute tactics risk damaging legitimate customer relationships and brand loyalty?
T.T.: A lot of merchants worry that fighting chargebacks is going to cost them customers, but that's not an effect we typically see among our clients. Some people who file illegitimate disputes are simply looking to take advantage of the system and were never good customers to begin with. Others are so dissatisfied with their experience that they won't be coming back regardless of the outcome.
In the long term, analyzing chargeback data can actually improve customer retention by identifying legitimate issues customers are having that the merchant might not otherwise know about. The key is looking at the evidence: purchase history, delivery records, customer service communications and patterns across previous disputes. At Chargeback Gurus, we analyze this kind of information to help merchants refine their dispute strategy and improve their overall operations.
In cases where the merchant has fallen short, they should make it right quickly. When the evidence shows that a dispute is invalid, they should challenge it with a well-documented response. That approach protects revenue while ensuring customers are treated fairly.
SJ: When payment leaders look at Chargeback Gurus, what is the core value proposition? How do you quantify the ROI for an enterprise merchant looking to safeguard revenue?
T.T.: We help merchants prevent chargebacks, recover revenue they're entitled to and increase the efficiency of that process. We also help them understand what's driving disputes so they can address recurring problems.
For enterprise merchants, I'd measure ROI against their starting point: additional dollars recovered, losses and fees avoided, and operational savings, minus the cost of the program.
SJ: Chargeback Gurus combines proprietary technology with deep dispute expertise. How does your platform blend automation and AI with human analysis to prevent disputes before they occur and win back lost revenue?
T.T.: AI enhances efficiency, while our experts enhance quality. Our proprietary local AI helps streamline the process of gathering evidence and creating dispute packages. It also analyzes data to provide merchants with additional insights. Our technology was created from the ground up by chargeback experts rather than being developed by software engineers trying to understand chargeback management.
Our experts use their knowledge of the merchant and the industry to shape dispute responses, test different approaches and review results. The goal is to present relevant evidence clearly and consistently in a way that achieves the best possible outcome for the merchant.
SJ: Looking ahead at emerging trends like agentic commerce and changing network rules, how should merchants adapt their risk strategies—and how is Chargeback Gurus evolving to keep them ahead of future fraud vectors?
T.T.: Right now, we're seeing several approaches to agentic commerce emerge. Tools like Google's AP2, Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol and Mastercard's Agent Pay are being developed to address various parts of the process, things like documenting customer intent and verifying legitimate agents.
For merchants, the practical question is whether that information will be available when a customer disputes a purchase. At Chargeback Gurus, we're working on incorporating these tools into our systems to ensure merchants have access to the best available evidence.
For now, merchants that want to accept agentic payments should be tracking these developments and ensuring their own systems are set up to work with these protocols.
Some enterprise merchants, such as Walmart, are even creating their own systems for agentic commerce, including authorizing third-party agents, setting spending limits, and ensuring agents can browse for and purchase products reliably.
